```{r}
##Load your input tree file##

#Read and Inspect Tree "For clades where only a single well-supported consensus phylogenetic tree containing all recognised species is available, ED2, and thus p, must still be calculated a large number of times to  adequately capture the uncertainty in p (100 < n ≤ 1000 to mirror approaches to capture phylogenetic uncertainty". So we must work with multi-phylo tree. dated_rand_sample_clements.tre <- dated taxon addition tree cloud, 100 topologies from the taxon addition treeset using random selections from the node dates age for each dated node calibration. First line is a header line containing the text "trees", followed by one newick tree per line.
#Downloaded from https://github.com/McTavishLab/AvesData/blob/main/Tree_versions/Aves_1.2/Clements2023/dated_sample_2023.tre
tree <- ape::read.tree("Data/tree/Clements2023_Aves1.3/dated_rand_sample_clements.tre")
str(tree)

# Loop over each tree in the multiPhylo object
for (i in 1:length(tree)) {

  # Check if single_tree is a phylo object
  if (!inherits(single_tree, "phylo")) {
    stop("Tree should be a phylo object.")
  }
  
  # Subset the tree
  tree_subset <- ape::drop.tip(single_tree, setdiff(single_tree$tip.label, species_in_pext))
  
# Store the subsetted tree in the list

}
```

```{r}
####### GE2 calculation Formula #########
#modified from https://github.com/rgumbs/EDGE2/ 

# Define pext values, excluding the DD and EX category
pext.vals <- data.frame(
  rl.cat = rev(c("CR", "EN", "VU", "NT", "LC")),
  pext   = rev(c(0.97, 0.97/2, 0.97/4, 0.97/8, 0.97/16))
)

# Function to calculate GE2 scores
GE.2.calc <- function(pext) {
  # Sample categories for LC to CR
  iucn <- sample(1:5, size = 1e6, replace = TRUE)
  data <- data.frame(species = 1:1e6, pext = pext$pext[iucn])
  data <- data[order(data$pext), ]
  data$rank <- seq_len(nrow(data))
  
  # Calculate the median rank for each category
  rank     <- c(0, with(data, tapply(rank, pext, median)))
  pext.tap <- c(0, pext$pext)
  
  # Fit the polynomial model
  rank.sq  <- rank^2
  rank.cub <- rank^3
  rank.qu  <- rank^4
  model    <- lm(pext.tap ~ rank + rank.sq + rank.cub + rank.qu)
  
  # Predict pext values
  data$rank.sq  <- data$rank^2
  data$rank.cub <- data$rank^3
  data$rank.qu  <- data$rank^4
  data$rank.pext <- predict(model, data)
  
  # Ensure pext values stay within [0.0001, 0.9999]
  data$rank.pext[data$rank.pext <= 0] <- 0.0001
  data$rank.pext[data$rank.pext >= 1] <- 0.9999
  
  # Create data frames for each IUCN category
  pext.LC <- data.frame(RL.cat = "LC", pext = data$rank.pext[data$pext == pext.tap[2]])
  pext.NT <- data.frame(RL.cat = "NT", pext = data$rank.pext[data$pext == pext.tap[3]])
  pext.VU <- data.frame(RL.cat = "VU", pext = data$rank.pext[data$pext == pext.tap[4]])
  pext.EN <- data.frame(RL.cat = "EN", pext = data$rank.pext[data$pext == pext.tap[5]])
  pext.CR <- data.frame(RL.cat = "CR", pext = data$rank.pext[data$pext == pext.tap[6]])
  
  # Combine all categories into one data frame
  pext.obj <- rbind(pext.CR, pext.EN, pext.VU, pext.NT, pext.LC)
  
  # Adjust pext values for each category to match target medians
  pext.obj.sample <- NULL
  for (i in unique(pext.obj$RL.cat)) {
    a <- pext.obj$pext[pext.obj$RL.cat == i]
    target_median <- pext$pext[pext$rl.cat == i]
    
    if (median(a) < target_median) {
      while (median(a) < target_median) {
        a <- a[-sample(1:length(a), 50, prob = rev(a))]
      }
    } else {
      while (median(a) > target_median) {
        a <- a[-sample(1:length(a), 50, prob = a)]
      }
    }
    
    pext.obj.sample <- rbind(pext.obj.sample, data.frame(RL.cat = i, pext = a))
  }
  
  
##For unassessed NE and DD species, p is drawn from the entire distribution completely at random under the assumption that, although we do not know where NE and DD species will be located along the curve, it must be at some point between 0 and 1, as with other extant species. Thus we generate highly uncertain scores for NE and DD species that have a median value equivalent to elevated extinction risk (VU) when taken over a large number of iterations
  
  # Set the target median for DD category
  target_median_dd <- 0.232  # The desired median for the Data Deficient (DD) category
  n <- 1e5  # Number of samples to generate for the DD category
  
  # Sample pext values from the entire existing distribution
  dd_values <- sample(pext.obj$pext, size = n, replace = TRUE)
  
  # Sort the sampled values and calculate the current median
  dd_values_sorted <- sort(dd_values)
  current_median <- median(dd_values_sorted)
  
  # Calculate the shift required to align the current median with the target median
  shift <- target_median_dd - current_median
  
  # Apply the shift and ensure all values remain within [0.0001, 0.9999]
  dd_values_shifted <- dd_values_sorted + shift
  dd_values_shifted[dd_values_shifted < 0.0001] <- 0.0001
  dd_values_shifted[dd_values_shifted > 0.9999] <- 0.9999
  
  # Add the adjusted DD category pext values to the final data frame
  pext.obj.sample <- rbind(
    pext.obj.sample,
    data.frame(RL.cat = "DD", pext = dd_values_shifted)
  )
  
  # Add EX category with fixed pext = 1 to make the total 1,000,000
  num_ex_values <- 1e6 - nrow(pext.obj.sample)
  pext.obj.sample <- rbind(
    pext.obj.sample,
    data.frame(RL.cat = "EX", pext = rep(1, num_ex_values))
  )
  
  # Return the updated data frame that now includes the DD and EX categories
  return(pext.obj.sample)
}

# Generate the pext samples including DD and EX categories
pext_sample <- GE.2.calc(pext.vals)

#Cat-count
table(pext_sample$RL.cat)

# Modify the IUCN category names
pext_sample_iucnmod <- pext_sample
pext_sample_iucnmod$RL.cat <- factor(pext_sample_iucnmod$RL.cat, 
                             levels = c("DD", "CR", "VU", "NT", "LC", "EN", "EX"),
                             labels = c("DD/NE", "CR", "VU", "NT", "LC", "EN", "EX"))

pext_sample_iucnmod <- pext_sample_iucnmod %>%
  mutate(RL.cat = reorder(RL.cat, pext, median, .desc = TRUE))

ggplot(pext_sample_iucnmod, aes(x = RL.cat, y = pext, fill = RL.cat)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  labs(
    title = "Boxplot of pext values (probabilities of extinction) for each IUCN Red List category",
    x = "IUCN Red List Category",
    y = "pext value (GE2)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  scale_fill_viridis_d()  # Use discrete viridis palette and reverse colors
```

```{r}
####### EDGE2 calculation Formula #########
#modified from https://github.com/rgumbs/EDGE2/

# Load required libraries
library(phylobase)
library(data.table)

# Function to reorder pext according to tree tip labels
into_order <- function(tree, pext) {
  new_pext <- pext[match(tree$tip.label, pext$species), ]
  return(new_pext)
}

# Function to reorder tree components
reorder_tree <- function(tree, ordering) {
  tree@edge.length <- tree@edge.length[ordering]
  tree@edge <- tree@edge[ordering, ]
  return(tree)
}

# EDGE2 Function
EDGE2_mod <- function(tree, pext) {
  
  names(pext) <- c("species", "pext")
  
  N_species <- length(tree$tip.label)
  N_nodes <- tree$Nnode
  N_tot <- N_species + N_nodes
  
  # Ensure extinction probabilities are given in the same order as tree$tip.label
  if (!identical(tree$tip.label, pext$species)) {
    pext <- into_order(tree, pext)
  }
  
  if (!inherits(tree, "phylo")) {
    tree <- as(tree, "phylo")
  }
  
  # Initialize data frames for results
  tree_dat <- data.frame(Species = as.character(tree$tip.label),
                         TBL = NA, 
                         pext = pext$pext, ED = NA, EDGE = NA)
  ePD.dat <- data.frame(PD = sum(tree$edge.length), ePDloss = NA)
  
  # Convert tree to phylo4 for edge operations
  tree <- as(tree, "phylo4")
  root <- rootNode(tree)
  nodes <- c(root, descendants(tree, root, "all"))
  
  # Reorder tree components for easier access
  ord <- order(nodes)
  tree <- reorder_tree(tree, ord)
  nodes <- nodes[ord]
  
  tree_dat$TBL <- tree@edge.length[1:N_species]
  
  node_data <- data.frame(Node = 1:N_tot, Pext = rep(1, N_tot), Edge_Sum = NA)
  node_data[1:N_species, 2] <- pext[, 2]
  
  # Assign the product of its descendant tips to each node
  for (i in c(1:length(tree@label), N_tot:(root + 1))) {         # for each node, beginning with tips
    anc <- tree@edge[i, 1]                                   # find ancestor of node
    node_data[anc, 2] <- node_data[anc, 2] * node_data[i, 2]   # multiply ancestor value by node "pext" 
  }

  # Multiply each edge length by the pext calculated above
  for (i in 1:length(nodes)) {
    tree@edge.length[i] <- tree@edge.length[i] * node_data[i, 2]
  }
  
  # Check for root edge length
  if (is.na(tree@edge.length[root])) {
    tree@edge.length[root] <- 0
  }
  
  node_data$Edge_Sum[root] <- tree@edge.length[root]
  
  # For each internal node, sum ancestral edge lengths
  for (i in (root + 1):N_tot) {
    ans <- tree@edge[i, 1]
    node_data$Edge_Sum[i] <- node_data$Edge_Sum[ans] + tree@edge.length[i]
  }
  
  # For each tip, sum ancestral edge lengths to find EDGE2 score
  for (i in 1:N_species) {
    ans <- tree@edge[i, 1]
    tree_dat$EDGE[i] <- node_data$Edge_Sum[ans] + tree@edge.length[i]
  }
  
  tree_dat$ED <- tree_dat$EDGE / tree_dat$pext
  
  # Reorder the tree for output
  tree <- reorder_tree(tree, order(ord))
  
  tree <- as(tree, "phylo")
  ePD.dat$ePDloss <- sum(tree$edge.length)
  
  edge.res <- list(tree_dat, tree, ePD.dat)
  return(edge.res)
}
```


```{r}
# Convert the pext_data to a data.table for efficient data manipulation
pext_data <- as.data.table(pext_data)

# Define a function to sample pext values based on IUCN categories - taking care of NE, CR(PE), CR(PEW), EW
sample_pext_values <- function(tree, pext_sample, pext_data) {
    # Extract species (tip labels) from the tree and convert them to character format
    species <- as.character(tree$tip.label)
    
    # Create a data frame to store the sampled pext values for each species
    sampled_pext <- data.frame(species = species, pext = NA)

    # Loop through each species in the tree's tip labels
    for (i in seq_along(species)) {
        current_species <- species[i]  # Get the current species
        
        # Retrieve the IUCN category for the current species from pext_data
        iucn_cat <- pext_data$IUCN_cat[pext_data$species == current_species]
        
        # Check if a corresponding IUCN category was found
        if (length(iucn_cat) == 0) {
            # If no category is found, issue a warning and skip to the next species
            warning(paste("No IUCN category found for species:", current_species))
            next
        }
        
        # Replace NE category with DD, since we did not add NE in our simulation, but it follows same logic as DD
        if (iucn_cat == "NE") {
            iucn_cat <- "DD"
        }
        
        # Treat CR(PE), CR(PEW), and EW as CR
        if (iucn_cat %in% c("CR(PE)", "CR(PEW)", "EW")) {
            iucn_cat <- "CR"
        }
        
        # Retrieve the pext values for the identified IUCN category from pext_sample
        pext_values <- pext_sample$pext[pext_sample$RL.cat == iucn_cat]
        
        # Check if there are available pext values for the category before sampling
        if (length(pext_values) > 0) {
            # Sample one pext value randomly and assign it to the current species
            sampled_pext$pext[i] <- sample(pext_values, 1)
        } else {
            # If no pext values are found for the IUCN category, assign NA
            sampled_pext$pext[i] <- NA
            # Issue a warning about the missing pext values for the species
            warning(paste("No pext values found for IUCN category:", iucn_cat, "for species:", current_species))
        }
    }
    
    # Return the data frame containing sampled pext values for each species
    return(sampled_pext)
}

# Initialize a list to store the results for each tree
results_list <- list()

# Loop over each tree in the list of trees
for (i in 1:length(trees)) {
    # Extract the current tree from the list
    tree <- trees[[i]]
    
    # Sample pext values for the current tree using the custom function
    sampled_pext <- sample_pext_values(tree, pext_sample, pext_data)
    
    # Calculate the EDGE2 scores using the sampled pext values for the tree
    edge2_results <- EDGE2_mod(tree, sampled_pext)
    
    # Extract the data frame containing the EDGE2 metrics (e.g., ED, EDGE, TBL)
    edge2_scores <- edge2_results[[1]]
    
    # Store the extracted scores in the results list for this tree
    results_list[[i]] <- edge2_scores
    
    # Save the EDGE2 scores to a CSV file for this tree
    write.csv(edge2_scores, 
              file = paste0("Result/v2023_aves1.3/edge2_scores_tree_", i, ".csv"), 
              row.names = FALSE)
}
```


```{r}
#To create a CSV file that stores the median ED, median EDGE, median pext, median TBL along with IQR values for each tip_label across the results from all 100 trees
# Define the directory where the CSV files are saved
result_dir <- "Result/v2023_aves1.3/"

# Get a list of all the CSV file paths
file_paths <- list.files(result_dir, pattern = "edge2_scores_tree_.*\\.csv", full.names = TRUE)

# Read each CSV file into a list
results_list <- lapply(file_paths, read.csv)

# Combine all results into one data frame
combined_results <- do.call(rbind, results_list)# Calculate median ED, EDGE, TBL, and pext for each tip_label

# Calculate median and interquartile range for ED, EDGE, TBL, and pext
summary_results <- combined_results %>%
  group_by(Species) %>%
  summarise(
    median_ED = median(ED),
    IQR_ED_25 = quantile(ED, 0.25),
    IQR_ED_75 = quantile(ED, 0.75),
    median_EDGE = median(EDGE),
    IQR_EDGE_25 = quantile(EDGE, 0.25),
    IQR_EDGE_75 = quantile(EDGE, 0.75),
    median_TBL = median(TBL),
    IQR_TBL_25 = quantile(TBL, 0.25),
    IQR_TBL_75 = quantile(TBL, 0.75),
    median_pext = median(pext),
    IQR_pext_25 = quantile(pext, 0.25),
    IQR_pext_75 = quantile(pext, 0.75)
  ) %>%
  rename(tip_label = Species)

# Save median results to a CSV file
write.csv(summary_results, file = "Result/v2023_aves1.3/Table_Median_IQR_EDGE2_scores_11017sp.csv", row.names = FALSE)
```
